persons.name: Gaṇeśvarānanda
persons.evidence: lalitāpura śrīmahābuddhayā paṃḍitātmaja śrīgaṇeśvarānandanaṃ ... siddhanaṃ coyā

notes: The colophon gives two dates: VS 1939 (−57 = 1882) and NS 1003 (+880 = 1883). They agree, because Pauṣa kṛṣṇa 3 of that year falls around Dec 1882–Jan 1883, most likely Jan 1883. The scribe is called 'paṃḍitātmaja', 'son of a paṇḍita'. The father is not named, so no relation is recorded. Mahābuddha is the Mahābauddha quarter of Patan. 'siddhanaṃ coyā' (Newari) means 'finished writing'. The catalogue lists King Bhūpatīndramalla, but no king is named in the colophon. He was a Bhaktapur king who died in 1722, so he cannot be the reigning king for a copy made in 1882/83; the catalogue entry is probably an error.
